qc.blur_rule: blur < 0.1 x blur_reference (median blur of clearly stained tiles)

tissue_mask.rule: fat-aware: saturation > 12 plus textured pale pixels (local SD > 4.0) within 40 px of stained tissue, on the 64x thumbnail; cell >= 50% tissue
tissue_mask.background_guard: < 10% colorful pixels and not labeled fat, or glass (blur < 0.0003 and < 30% colorful), or glass / ink by texture (edges < 0.02 or structure_cov < 0.4 or pen-ink colors)

blood_check.rule: MUSK p_blood >= 0.5 and not labeled fat

caveats: Decision support only: not a diagnosis and not a treatment recommendation.
One slide is a 2D snapshot: 'direction' means where the front faces in this section, not where it will grow.
T stage needs more than one slide: the depth line is a 'consistent with' hint, never a stage.
H&E shows where lymphocytes sit, not their type (CD8 vs CD4) or what they are doing.
The map works at 112 µm tiles: single budding cells and tumor pieces smaller than ~0.3 mm are invisible to it.
Flags are 'look here' hints from text matching and shape rules; expect false alarms.
Pushing vs infiltrative cut-offs were set from by-eye calls on slide thumbnails (agreed on 15 of 19 held-out TCGA slides), not checked by a pathologist.
Some risk-map points are placeholders until the features doc's points table is copied in.
This slide has 9 tissue sections; the analysis covers the one with the largest tumor.
The outer edge may be a cut surface rather than serosa, and the rectum below the peritoneal fold has no serosa: check before calling pT4a.
